text: In 1886, Coca-Cola sold nine servings of its drinks per day in its first year; now it has over 2.2 billion servings consumed daily worldwide, which is about 25,500 every second.
During conversations, each speaker's turn averages 2 seconds with a 200-millisecond pause in between. This quick transition is nearly universal across cultures.
On June 4, 1923, jockey Frank Hayes suffered a fatal heart attack mid-race, but his horse, Sweet Kiss, finished and won, making him the only jockey to win a race posthumously.
Two diseases have been successfully eradicated: smallpox in 1980 after the last case in 1977, and rinderpest in 2011 after the last case in 2001.
The difference between mist and fog comes down to visibility: if you can't see farther than 0.6 miles (1 km), it's fog; if you can, it's mist.
According to the FDA, Kraft Singles are labeled as "pasteurized prepared cheese product" due to containing under 51% real cheese.
Perfluorohexane dissolves large amounts of oxygen, allowing animals to survive underwater by inhaling oxygenated liquid.
In the 1870s, 37 cats were trained to deliver mail in Liège, Belgium, but the experiment was short-lived due to inefficiency, with most cats taking up to a day for deliveries.
In 1889, Margherita pizza was crafted to honor Queen Margherita, using ingredients that symbolize the Italian flag's colors: tomato, mozzarella, and basil.
Nestlé produces KitKat and Rolo globally, with the exception of the U.S., where these products are manufactured by their competitor, Hershey's.
Dexter Holland, lead singer of The Offspring, earned a Ph.D. in molecular biology from the University of Southern California, graduating in May 2017 while still active in the band.
Shakira was turned down by her school choir in second grade, with her teacher criticizing her strong vibrato as sounding "like a goat."
